subject: Clarification on PHI handling and BAA scope for HealthGrid
messages:
From: Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@healthgrid.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2026 17:12:00 -0500
Subject: PHI handling and BAA request – initial info

Hi Vanessa,

Hope you're well. We're starting our security and legal review for a potential pilot of Redwood to power a patient messaging feature. A few questions up front so our procurement and privacy teams can triage:

- Can Redwood accept PHI (patient identifiers + notes) for processing via the hosted API, or is PHI limited to Dedicated/Private deployments only?
- If PHI is allowed, what is the exact scope where Redwood would be a "business associate" (e.g., tokenization only, full-text processing, embeddings storage, logs)?
- Please share your standard BAA, and any supporting artifacts (data flow diagram, DPIA summary, SOC 2 Type II report or SIG/CAIQ where available).

I've attached our standard BAA request form for initial intake (BAA_request_form_HG_20260115.pdf). We also need to understand whether audit logs, request/response bodies, or KV cache could contain PHI and how long those artifacts are retained by default.

Can you confirm next steps and an estimated timeline to get a draft BAA in DocuSign?

Thanks,
Angela Ruiz
Head of Procurement
HealthGrid Medical Systems

--
Attachment: BAA_request_form_HG_20260115.pdf

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2026 18:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: PHI handling and BAA request – initial info

Hi Angela — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marcus (Security) and Mina (Legal) to confirm technical and contract scope. Quick answers while they jump in: 

- Short answer: PHI is not permitted on Redwood's multi-tenant hosted API unless data is de-identified. For workloads that require handling PHI, we support Dedicated and Private deployments under a signed BAA.
- Scope: Under a BAA, we can be a business associate for processing (e.g., generating responses, embeddings) when the customer places workloads on Dedicated or Private instances. Logs, KV caches, and any persisted request/response bodies are controlled by the deployment mode and customer settings — we can configure retention and disable certain caches for BAA-covered workloads.

Marcus and Mina: can you confirm the default retention windows for request/response bodies and audit logs, and whether we can provide a concise DPIA summary for HealthGrid?

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus to send a short technical note (dataflow + retention/encryption) and the DPIA summary.
2) Mina to circulate our standard BAA and intake the redlines; we can prepare DocuSign once we align scope.
3) Schedule a 30-min call to walk through redlines and technical controls.

Would early next week work from your side?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@healthgrid.com>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Jan 2026 09:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: PHI handling and BAA request – technical details and DPIA summary

Thanks Vanessa — hi Angela.

Following up with the technical details you requested. High-level summary first, then specifics we can include in the DPIA summary: 

Summary:
- PHI processing is supported only on Dedicated (redwood-managed reserved GPU pools) or Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments after a signed BAA and configuration review. Our public hosted API is multi-tenant and meant for non-PHI or de-identified data.
- Encryption: All data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest encryption is AES-256. Customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations are available for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Logging & caches:
  - Request/response bodies: Persisted only if customer enables logging/ingestion. For BAA deployments we default to disabled logging; if enabled we can limit retention to a configurable policy (default for BAA: 30 days, can be shorter on request).
  - KV cache / prefix cache: By default used for performance. For PHI workloads we can disable KV persistence or restrict it to memory-only; this is configurable per-deployment.
  - Audit logs: Immutable audit trail of administrative actions is retained 365 days by default for Dedicated/Private; we can export to customer S3 for longer-term retention under their control.
- Model artifacts & embeddings: Persistent embeddings storage is off by default for BAA workloads; if enabled, embeddings are stored in an encrypted datastore and can be configured to purge on a customer schedule.
- Access controls: RBAC, mTLS between service components, and optional VPC peering for Private installs.

Attachments: included a simple dataflow diagram that contrasts Hosted vs Dedicated/Private (redwood-dataflow_dedicated_vs_hosted.png). I'll also prepare the DPIA summary and a short checklist of controls we'll include in the BAA.

We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and SIG/CAIQ artifacts under NDA; Mina can advise on the sharing workflow.

Action items:
- Vanessa: propose meeting windows.
- Angela: confirm whether you want a Dedicated or Private deployment for the pilot (or if you prefer to start with de-identified hosted traffic).
- Mina: please confirm the BAA sharing steps.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
